real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates eased to 7.54% from a near three year high as hiring slowed to 29,000 jobs in September.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage rates eased from a near three year high. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year was 7.54% on Thursday, down 0.06 from Wednesday's 7.60%, and the 15-year is 7.18%. On our five city median of $1,079,500 with 20% down, principal and interest come to $6,062 a month, $36 less than Wednesday and still $380 more than when September began at 6.89%.

This morning's jobs report is the kind of news that can move rates. Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August were revised down by a combined 60,000. The 10-Year Treasury, which mortgage rates tend to follow, was near 5.24% at 8:00 AM PT, about where it closed Thursday, so the report has not moved rates yet.

Locally, the five city ledger edged up to 679 from 675 and the board wide table rose 28 to 2,700, with 189 brand new listings, up from 166 on Thursday.

What this means for you: buyers who stepped back at 7.60% should keep a preapproval current, because on the median home every quarter point off the rate is worth about $147 a month. Sellers should price for today's rates, not tomorrow's; 140 of the ledger's 604 homes on the market have been listed 60 days or longer.

• Board wide: 2,700 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 161 coming soon and 189 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 679 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 604 are on the market and 75 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 244 live, 193 active, 30 coming soon, 20 brand new and 1 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,249,495 at $781 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 30 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 179, Milpitas 107, Newark 88, Union City 61.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,079,500 at $675 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 140 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Thursday, October 1 at the closing bell. Friday is live: at 8:00 AM PT the S&P was 7,737.43 (+0.93%), the Dow 51,198.27 (+0.53%) and the Nasdaq 27,266.38 (+1.47%).
stocks.news:
Stocks inched higher Thursday to open the fourth quarter, and Friday is stronger so far: at 8:00 AM PT the S&P 500 was up 0.93% and the Nasdaq up 1.47%.

Today's first chart is Nike. Revenue fell 4% to $11.2 billion in the quarter ended August 31, and Greater China fell 26% excluding currency moves (22% in dollars), leaving it smaller than Asia Pacific and Latin America; a year ago it was larger. North America grew 2%. Nike expects revenue for the fiscal year to fall by a high single digit percentage, and the shares are down 5.89% this morning after closing Thursday at $35.15, already their lowest close since 2016. The turnaround is still at the starting line.

feature_image.alt: Bar chart of Nike revenue change by region from a year earlier, currency-neutral, for the quarter ended August 31, 2026: Greater China down 26% ($1.18 billion, from $1.51 billion, down 22% in dollars), EMEA down 5% ($3.18 billion, from $3.33 billion), APLA flat ($1.46 billion, from $1.49 billion, down 2% in dollars) and North America up 2% ($5.13 billion, from $5.02 billion). Total revenue was $11.21 billion, down 4% in dollars and 5% currency-neutral.
feature_image.caption: Nike's Greater China revenue fell 26% excluding currency moves and is now smaller than its Asia Pacific and Latin America business. North America grew 2%.
feature_image.source: Source: NIKE, Inc. fiscal 2027 first quarter results, Form 8-K filed October 1, 2026.

economy.commentary:
Today's second chart started as the ISM factory survey making the rounds: its index was 54.5 in September, the ninth straight month of growth, with the prices gauge jumping to 77.9 from 71.1. ISM does not allow charts built from its index, so we drew the same story from public jobs data. Factories added 9,000 jobs in September, a fourth straight monthly gain, and 72,000 since December.

The local picture splits. Factory jobs in the San Jose metro rose 1.4% in the year to August, while the Oakland-Fremont area, which covers Alameda and Contra Costa counties, lost 5.5%. Its 93,300 factory jobs are the fewest for an August since 2016, down from 113,500 at the September 2022 peak.

The wider jobs report was soft: hourly pay rose 3.0% in a year, below the 3.4% rise in consumer prices. In Europe, today's flash estimate put euro area inflation at 3.8% in September, up from 3.2%, led by energy at 18.8%. December gold settled up 0.37% and silver up 1.01%. Brent's December contract jumped 4.37% Thursday to $102.31 and is giving back part of it this morning.

feature_image.alt: Two panel chart. Left: U.S. manufacturing employment, seasonally adjusted, October 2025 to September 2026, falling to a December low of 12,580,000 and rising to 12,652,000 in September, up 72,000 since December. Right: factory jobs in August 2026 compared with a year earlier, not seasonally adjusted: San Jose metro up 1.4% (131,400 jobs), United States up 0.3%, California down 1.2% and the Oakland-Fremont area down 5.5% (93,300 jobs, highlighted).
feature_image.caption: U.S. factory jobs have risen four months in a row, but the Oakland-Fremont area, Alameda and Contra Costa counties, has 5.5% fewer than a year ago.
feature_image.source: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, national through September and metro through August 2026.
